gates.title: Direction recovery and unit-vector normalization

canonical_concepts.statement: A reference angle does not determine physical direction without the signed component quadrant.
i-hat/j-hat coefficients are the signed x/y components in the same basis.
Dividing a nonzero vector by its magnitude preserves direction and produces magnitude one.

external_prerequisites.statement: Recover a reference angle from a valid trigonometric ratio.

relations.expression: theta_ref = atan(|Ay/Ax|); physical direction = theta_ref placed by sign(Ax), sign(Ay)
relations.meaning: Signed components determine a reference angle and physical quadrant for a nonzero 2-D vector.
conditions: The x and y axes are perpendicular and their positive directions are declared.
Inverse trigonometry supplies a reference/principal angle; the component signs determine the physical quadrant.
If Ax=0, read the vertical direction directly from the sign of Ay rather than dividing by Ax.

relations.expression: |A| = sqrt(Ax^2 + Ay^2); A_hat = (Ax i-hat + Ay j-hat)/|A|
relations.meaning: Dividing a nonzero vector by its magnitude preserves direction and produces a dimensionless vector of magnitude one.
conditions: The x and y axes are perpendicular and use the same physical unit.
The vector magnitude is nonzero before division.
The same positive magnitude divides every signed component, so direction is preserved.

validity_conditions: Axes are declared before signs/direction are interpreted.
Inverse trig is a Mathematics bridge, not silently self-certified by Physics.

reasoning_sequence.action: Retain signed components and identify the requested representation.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Direction and notation meaning are lost if component signs or basis are discarded.

reasoning_sequence.action: Recover direction, translate notation or normalize using the declared relation.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Each operation preserves the same underlying vector information under explicit conditions.

reasoning_sequence.action: Use sign, round-trip or magnitude-one checks.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Representation invariants independently detect setup and sign errors.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A raw inverse-tangent output fully determines vector direction.
misconceptions.counterexample: Vectors in quadrants I and III can share the same positive component ratio magnitude.
misconceptions.repair: Retain the component signs and use inverse trig only for a reference angle.

problem_families.title: Resultant direction, i/j notation and 2-D unit-direction questions
hidden_invariants: i/j coefficients round-trip to the same pair.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from the first symbol of the first relation.
